memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Aaron then brought the offering that was for the people. He took the goat for the people's sin offering and slaughtered it and offered it for a sin offering as he did with the first one." - Lev 9:15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Having dealt with himself, Aaron turns to the people. And the wording is precise: as he did with the first one.

The same care. The same procedure. The same seriousness.

Aaron did not treat the nation's offering as routine after handling his own. He did not become efficient about it, hurrying through because he had already done this once today.

There is a warning here for anyone who handles holy things regularly. Familiarity dulls. The pastor who has preached a thousand sermons, the musician who has led worship for years, the parent who has prayed at a thousand meals — all can arrive at a place where sacred things are handled competently but not reverently.

The remedy is not manufactured emotion. It is remembering what is actually happening. Aaron was standing between a holy God and a sinful nation. Nothing about that was ordinary, however many times he did it.

Whatever you do for God this week — however often you have done it before — someone's soul may be involved. Handle it as you did the first one.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Has something sacred become routine for me through repetition?
2. What would it look like to approach a familiar spiritual duty with fresh reverence?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, forgive me where familiarity has made me casual with holy things. Restore my reverence for what I handle every day. Amen.
